script.title: Why New York's Most Famous Resident Was Originally Copper
script.hook_text: She was originally a different color
sentences: New York's most famous resident was originally a different color.
In the 1870s, Frédéric Bartholdi used thin copper to keep her lightweight.
This allowed the statue to be shipped from France in crates.
Her torch arm arrived first and sat in a Manhattan park for years.
Imagine walking past a giant disembodied hand on your morning commute.
The interior metal framework was even designed by Gustave Eiffel.
President Grover Cleveland dedicated the monument in 1886.
Because she is copper-clad, the statue once had a bright metallic look.
How would New York look with a shiny copper giant in the harbor?
script.description: The Statue of Liberty wasn't always green. Discover how a French sculptor used copper sheets to build a New York icon.

claims_en: The Statue of Liberty was originally a different color than it is today.
Frédéric Bartholdi used copper to build the statue to keep it lightweight.
The statue was shipped from France to the United States in crates.
The torch-bearing arm was displayed in Madison Square Park from 1876 to 1882.
Gustave Eiffel designed the internal metal framework for the statue.
President Grover Cleveland presided over the dedication in 1886.
The statue is clad in copper.
The statue originally had a bright metallic appearance.
